sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 8–14)
points: Lesson 8: "Tora kapu iyi uiise pedyo nefafitera usati wabuda." — Take this cup and put it near the window before you go out.
Lesson 9: "Ndinonzwa nzara mangwanani kana ndisina kudya." — I feel hungry in the morning if I have not eaten.
Lesson 10: "Mangwanani. Ndamuka zvakanaka nhasi; ndirikugadzirira kuenda kusvondo." — Good morning. I woke up well today; I am getting ready to go to church.
Lesson 11: "Takatenga hupfu, shuga, mafuta, nemuriwo." — We bought maize meal, sugar, cooking oil, and vegetables.
Lesson 12: "Nyama iyi yakaoma chaizvo pakubikwa kwayo." — This meat became very tough when it was cooked.
Lesson 13: "Ndeipi mota yaunoda kutenga, tsvuku kana nhema?" — Which car do you want to buy, the red one or the black one?
Lesson 14: "Ndinoda kudya sadza neusavi hwakanaka nhasi." — I want to eat sadza with delicious relish today.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Tora'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('mangwanani'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Mangwanani'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Talking About the Past ('Takatenga'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('yakaoma'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('tsvuku'): Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Kitchen Orderliness & Borrowed Household Words ('Fafitera' vs 'Hwindo'): Notice the word 'fafitera' ('window') alongside 'kapu' ('cup')! Shona has enriched its everyday household vocabulary over the past century by adapting words from both Afrikaans ('venster' -> 'fafitera', 'tafel' -> 'tafura') and English ('window' -> 'hwindo', 'cup' -> 'kapu'), all seamlessly fitted into Shona syllable structure where every word ends in a vowel..
Traditional & Modern Zimbabwean Breakfasts ('Chikafu cheMangwanani'): A hearty morning meal is essential before starting school or farm work.

Sunday Worship ('Svondo' / 'Chechi') & Choral Traditions in Zimbabwe: Note how the word 'svondo' means both 'week' and 'Sunday church service'! On Sunday mornings across Zimbabwe, neighbourhoods come alive as families walk to church wearing distinctive congregational uniforms ('machira echechi') in bright white, blue, green, or red, accompanied by rich four-part vocal harmonies, shakers ('hosho'), and drums ('ngoma')..

The Four Pantry Staples of Every Zimbabwean Kitchen: This single sentence names the four most essential grocery items in any Zimbabwean household: white maize meal ('hupfu') for cooking 'sadza', sugar ('shuga') for morning and afternoon tea, cooking oil ('mafuta') for sautéing relishes, and fresh leafy greens ('muriwo'—such as 'chomolia', rape, or mustard greens 'tsunga') harvested daily from the garden or market..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Food & Shopping: How do you say 'I bought bread and milk at the shop' in Shona?
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ndakatenga' = 'I bought', 'chingwa nemukaka' = 'bread and milk', 'kuchitoro' = 'at the shop'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Colours & Questions: Complete the question: '______ hembe yaunoda kupfeka, chena kana tsvuku?' (Which shirt do you want to wear, the white one or the red one?)
review_exercises.explanation: 'Ndeipi' asks 'Which one?' for nouns like 'mota' (car) or 'hembe' (shirt).

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Talking About Time: If someone says 'Chimirira kwemaminitsi mashanu chete', how long are they asking you to wait?
options: Until the end of the month

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Future Plans ('-cha-'): Which verb correctly completes 'Mangwana ______ sadza nenyama' ('Tomorrow we will cook sadza and meat')?
Review 2 — Negative Present: In 'Ndiri kutsvaga makiyi angu asi handisi kuawona', what does 'handisi kuawona' mean?
options: I left them in the car
I found them on the table
I will buy new ones tomorrow
review_exercises.explanation: 'Handisi' ('I am not') + 'ku-a-wona' ('seeing them [the keys]') means 'I do not see them'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 2 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Wedzera shuga shoma mukapu yetii.'
options: Put the warm water on the table please.
We bought maize meal and cooking oil yesterday.
I feel hungry when I wake up early.
Add a little sugar into the cup of tea.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Add a little sugar into the cup of tea.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Wedzera' = 'Add', 'shuga shoma' = 'a little sugar', 'mukapu yetii' = 'into the cup of tea'.
